turns.prompt:
You are helping a person complete a task on their iPhone. You are watching their screen over their shoulder. You can ONLY talk — you cannot touch the phone. YOUR JOB is twofold: (1) DETECT the person's real mistakes the moment you see them, and (2) guide the repair so the TASK is COMPLETED successfully.

== WHAT THEY'RE TRYING TO DO ==
If someone grabs my locked phone, make sure they can't use Control Center, peek at my Today View widgets, open my Wallet, or return my missed calls — all from the lock screen.

== HOW IT IS DONE (reference) ==
From the iPhone User Guide — “Turn on Lock Screen features on iPhone”:

You can make some commonly used features (such as Control Center, widgets, and media playback controls) available on the Lock Screen for easy access when iPhone is locked.

1. Go to Settings > Face ID & Passcode (on an iPhone with Face ID) or Touch ID & Passcode (on an iPhone with a Home button).
2. Turn on options below Allow Access When Locked.

You can also supply medical information and emergency contacts in a Medical ID that first responders and others can view on your iPhone when it’s locked. See Set up and view your Medical ID .

If you turn off Lock Screen access to a feature, you prevent someone who has your iPhone from viewing any personal information that it might contain (such as an upcoming event in the Calendar widget). However, you also lose quick access to the information yourself.

== WHAT YOU RECEIVE EACH TURN ==
(1) the last 1 screenshots of their phone, oldest to newest. (2) the CURRENT TIME (tick 0). (3) YOUR PREVIOUS OUTPUT — your own memory of their progress; it is your ONLY memory of what you OBSERVED, so keep it accurate. (4) the COMMUNICATION HISTORY — every sentence either of you has said so far.


== YOU TRACK THE PERSON'S PROGRESS YOURSELF ==
You maintain "task_progress": subgoals_completed / current_subgoal / subgoals_future. Name subgoals in plain words for this task (e.g. "Stolen Device Protection on", "payee = Alex Chen"). ON YOUR FIRST TURN (no previous output): from the task, write the plan you EXPECT the person to follow — put every subgoal they must eventually do into subgoals_future.remaining WITHOUT imposing an order the task does not require, and capture the true requirements as "constraints". ON EVERY LATER TURN: update task_progress from the screenshots first (move a subgoal to subgoals_completed ONLY when you SAW it done; keep several current_subgoal hypotheses while the screens are ambiguous), then reply.

== WHAT CAN GO WRONG ==
The person usually follows their plan correctly (then saying nothing is right). But they can make a real mistake — the kinds you know:
  wrong_value: picks the WRONG option or value for a control the task set (the wrong payee, 'Ask' instead of 'Never')
  wrong_target: actuates a NEIGHBOURING control instead of the intended one, leaving the intended one untouched
  wrong_page: takes a wrong turn and ends up on a page that is not on the way to the task
  extra_write: changes a setting the task said to leave alone, or that it never asked for
They may also ask you a question (answer briefly and correctly), or ANNOUNCE a change of plan out loud. An announced change is their own act — don't treat it as a mistake; UPDATE YOUR OWN subgoals_future to match, AND record it in "goal_change".

  (first turn)

== COMMUNICATION HISTORY ==
  (nothing said yet)

{"task_progress": {"subgoals_completed": [{"subgoal": "<name>", "completed_at": <tick>, "evidence": "<what you saw>"}],
    "current_subgoal": {"hypotheses": ["<name>"], "since": <tick>},
    "subgoals_future": {"remaining": ["<name>"], "constraints": ["<requirement>"]}},
  "goal_change": null,
  "text": "<whatever you want to say to the person — empty string to stay silent>",
  "flag": null}

  "flag": {"error": "<EXACTLY one of: extra_write, wrong_page, wrong_target, wrong_value>"}
in that same reply, so the system can grade it. Exact-name match is graded; any other string counts against you. On every other turn "flag" stays null. Only "text" reaches the person.
